syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: A Simple Economy

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish goods, services and resources as used in the chapter.
Explain why limited resources force individuals to make choices.
Identify allocation of resources and distribution of output as basic economic problems.

topics.title: Central Problems of an Economy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how scarcity of resources with competing uses gives rise to the problem of choice.
Classify economic decisions under what to produce, how to produce and for whom to produce.

topics.title: Production Possibility Frontier and Opportunity Cost

concepts.learning_objective: Define the production possibility set of an economy.
Interpret points on, inside and outside the production possibility frontier.
Calculate the opportunity cost of an additional unit of a good from a production possibilities schedule.

topics.title: Organisation of Economic Activities

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how a central authority solves the central problems in a centrally planned economy.
Explain how price signals coordinate economic activities in a market economy.
Describe why real-world economies are mixed economies.

topics.title: Positive and Normative Economics

concepts.learning_objective: Identify positive economic analysis as the study of how mechanisms function.
Identify normative economic analysis as the evaluation of whether outcomes are desirable.
Explain why the distinction between positive and normative analysis is not sharp.

topics.title: Microeconomics and Macroeconomics

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the subject matter of microeconomics.
Describe the aggregate questions studied in macroeconomics.

topics.title: Utility and Cardinal Utility Analysis

concepts.learning_objective: Define total and marginal utility and compute one from the other.
Explain the law of diminishing marginal utility and how it explains a downward sloping demand curve.

topics.title: Ordinal Utility Analysis and Indifference Curves

concepts.learning_objective: Define and calculate the marginal rate of substitution and state the law of diminishing MRS.
Explain the shape and features of indifference curves and the indifference map.
Apply the idea of monotonic preferences to rank consumption bundles.

topics.title: The Consumer's Budget

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the budget set and budget line, their intercepts and slope.
Analyse how changes in income and prices change the budget line.

topics.title: Optimal Choice of the Consumer

concepts.learning_objective: Locate the consumer's optimum bundle as the tangency of the budget line with an indifference curve.
Explain why MRS must equal the price ratio at the optimum and how a consumer adjusts when it does not.

topics.title: Demand, Law of Demand and Types of Goods

concepts.learning_objective: State the law of demand and interpret the demand function and a linear demand curve.
Distinguish normal, inferior and Giffen goods using income and substitution effects.
Distinguish substitutes from complements by the effect of a related good's price.

topics.title: Shifts in Demand and Market Demand

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a movement along the demand curve from a shift of the demand curve.
Derive market demand by horizontal summation of individual demand curves.

topics.title: Price Elasticity of Demand and its Measurement

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate price elasticity of demand by the percentage method and classify it.
Analyse how elasticity varies along a linear demand curve and identify constant elasticity curves.

topics.title: Determinants of Elasticity, and Elasticity and Expenditure

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how necessities, luxuries and close substitutes affect price elasticity.
Predict the change in expenditure on a good from its price elasticity.

topics.title: Production Function

concepts.learning_objective: Define the production function as the maximum output obtainable from given inputs and use it to compute output.
Explain that a production function assumes efficient use of inputs and is defined for a given technology.

topics.title: The Short Run, the Long Run and Isoquants

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the short run from the long run by whether all inputs can be varied.
Explain an isoquant and why it slopes downward when marginal products are positive.

topics.title: Total Product, Average Product and Marginal Product

concepts.learning_objective: Define total, average and marginal product of a variable input.
Calculate TP, AP and MP schedules from one another.

topics.title: Law of Variable Proportions and Shapes of Product Curves

concepts.learning_objective: State and explain the law of variable proportions using changing factor proportions.
Explain the shapes of the TP, AP and MP curves and the relationship between AP and MP.

topics.title: Returns to Scale

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish constant, increasing and decreasing returns to scale.
Identify returns to scale of a Cobb-Douglas production function from the sum of its exponents.

topics.title: Cost Function and Short Run Cost Concepts

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the cost function as the least cost of producing each output level.
Calculate TFC, TVC, TC, AFC, AVC, SAC and SMC and relate them to one another.

topics.title: Shapes of the Short Run Cost Curves

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the shapes of the TFC and AFC curves and why AFC is a rectangular hyperbola.
Explain why SMC, AVC and SAC are U-shaped and where SMC cuts AVC and SAC.

topics.title: Long Run Costs

concepts.learning_objective: Define long run average and marginal cost and explain why there is no fixed cost in the long run.
Relate the U-shape of the LRAC curve to increasing, constant and decreasing returns to scale.

chapters.title: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition

topics.title: Perfect competition: defining features and price-taking

concepts.learning_objective: State the four defining features of a perfectly competitive market and why each matters.
Explain why firms and buyers in a perfectly competitive market behave as price-takers.

topics.title: Revenue: total, average and marginal revenue

concepts.learning_objective: Compute TR, AR and MR for a price-taking firm and show that MR = AR = p.
Interpret the TR curve and the price line as the perfectly elastic demand curve facing a firm.

topics.title: Conditions for profit maximisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why profit is maximised where price equals marginal cost.
Explain why marginal cost must be non-decreasing at the profit-maximising output.
Apply the conditions p >= AVC in the short run and p >= AC in the long run to the decision to produce.

topics.title: Short run and long run supply curve of a firm

concepts.learning_objective: Derive the short run supply curve of a firm from its SMC and AVC curves.
Derive the long run supply curve of a firm from its LRMC and LRAC curves.

topics.title: Shut down point, normal profit and break-even point

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the short run and long run shut down points of a firm.
Distinguish normal profit, super-normal profit and the break-even point.
Calculate the opportunity cost of an activity as the gain foregone from the next best alternative.

topics.title: Determinants of a firm's supply curve

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how technological progress shifts a firm's supply curve.
Explain how a change in input prices shifts a firm's supply curve.
Analyse how a unit tax changes a firm's cost curves and long run supply curve.

topics.title: Market supply curve

concepts.learning_objective: Derive the market supply curve by horizontally summing the supply curves of individual firms.
Explain how a change in the number of firms shifts the market supply curve.

topics.title: Price elasticity of supply

concepts.learning_objective: Define and calculate the price elasticity of supply by the percentage method.
Use the geometric method to judge the elasticity of straight line supply curves.

topics.title: Equilibrium, excess demand and excess supply

concepts.learning_objective: Define market equilibrium, equilibrium price and equilibrium quantity in a perfectly competitive market.
Identify excess demand and excess supply at a price and describe equilibrium as zero excess demand and zero excess supply.
Explain how the 'Invisible Hand' moves price towards equilibrium when the market is out of equilibrium.

topics.title: Equilibrium with a fixed number of firms

concepts.learning_objective: Show that with a fixed number of firms, equilibrium lies at the intersection of the market demand and market supply curves.
Calculate equilibrium price, equilibrium quantity and excess demand or supply from linear demand and supply equations.

topics.title: Wage determination in the labour market

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a profit-maximising firm hires labour until the wage equals the marginal revenue product of labour and why labour demand slopes downward.
Explain the backward-bending individual labour supply curve and the upward-sloping market supply of labour.
Describe how the wage rate is determined where labour demand by firms equals labour supply by households.

topics.title: Shifts in demand and supply

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how a shift in the demand curve changes equilibrium price and quantity with a fixed number of firms.
Analyse how a shift in the supply curve changes equilibrium price and quantity with a fixed number of firms.
Predict which effects of simultaneous shifts in demand and supply are certain and which depend on the size of the shifts.

topics.title: Market equilibrium with free entry and exit

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why free entry and exit make the equilibrium price equal to the minimum average cost of firms.
Calculate the equilibrium quantity and the equilibrium number of firms under free entry and exit.
Compare the effect of a demand shift under free entry and exit with that under a fixed number of firms.

topics.title: Applications: price ceiling and price floor

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the effects of a price ceiling below the equilibrium price, including shortage, rationing and black markets.
Explain the effects of a price floor above the equilibrium price, including excess supply and government purchase of the surplus.
